# 1.33.0: Documents and files in the chat, tasks for later, middle-click scrolling

Settings, keys and conversations from earlier versions are read as they are.

## Documents and files

- **The chat reads Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF** on this computer: Word as numbered
  paragraphs, Excel as sheet rows with cell addresses, PowerPoint and PDF page by page. A long
  document comes in parts, and the model reads further only when it needs to.
- **Attached documents reach the model as text** with a short table of contents, so a big file
  no longer fills the conversation. Earlier versions unpacked attachments into plain-text copies
  in the Windows temp folder, outside the program's encryption; that no longer happens, and the
  old copies are deleted on the first start.
- **New tools:** `edit_file` changes a text file or a Word document by exact replacement, the way
  code editors with AI do it; `create_folder`; `create_document` makes Word, Excel, PDF, HTML or
  text files from Markdown or from rows of cells; `edit_document` changes Word paragraphs, Excel
  cells and sheets, and keeps or joins PDF pages; `save_image` saves a generated or downloaded
  picture. PowerPoint is read-only.
- **Every result comes back with its path.** The file card in the answer opens the file; a
  right-click shows it in its folder, copies the file itself (so it can be pasted into a
  messenger or Explorer) or saves a copy elsewhere. You can also drag the card out of the window.
- **Edits don't work from an old version.** The model can change a file only after reading it in
  the same chat, and only if nobody changed it since; otherwise it is told to read it again.
  Several edits of one file in the same step no longer overwrite each other.
- **Old versions don't confuse the model.** Text of files that were changed later, long old
  arguments, documents from earlier messages and earlier versions of the same code block are sent
  to the model as short notes. The conversation you see and the saved chat stay as they were.
- **Excel and Word files stay healthy.** Cell formatting survives edits, Excel doesn't offer to
  repair a file after its formulas change, a renamed sheet takes its references along, and Word
  documents keep their structure and heading styles.
- **The chat does documents itself, whatever their size, and does not hand the work back to you.**
  When you ask for a file, you get the file, not instructions for making it yourself. The agent
  steps in only for a part the chat's own tools cannot do.
- **The program does the volume and the arithmetic.** An Excel table that follows a rule is
  written from one formula or one number series filled over a whole range, the way dragging works
  in Excel, and the program calculates the formulas as it writes the file. So a multiplication
  table up to 150 is three lines for the model, not 22,500 numbers it might get wrong, and the
  workbook shows its values even before Excel opens it.
- **A document can be made from another one in a single step:** a PDF or Word file from an Excel
  workbook (with the formula results), a PDF from a Word file, presentation, CSV or text. Nothing
  is retyped.
- A document too big for one answer is built in parts into the same file: Word and PDF get new
  content at the end, Excel gets new rows. A table wider than the page is printed in blocks of
  columns, each repeating the first column, instead of running off the edge.
- **Documents made by the AI need no permission.** A new document, picture or folder is created
  without asking anywhere except the Windows, program and application-data folders, other users'
  profiles and network shares, and a document the AI made can be changed later without asking too,
  even after you edited it yourself. Changing your own files still asks first, and so does any
  script or program file, wherever it goes. *Ask about everything* in Settings → Security still
  asks about all of it.
- **Where files go.** A relative path means your Downloads folder. None of the writing tools can
  touch the program's own data folder, whatever path they are given.
- Saving a document no longer fails when an antivirus scans the file at that moment.

## Tasks for later

- **The chat can do things later.** Ask it to remind you, to run a task with the agent, to run a
  command, or to reopen the programs that were open when the computer was turned off. The model
  can also offer to follow up by itself when it is clearly useful, and it always tells you what
  it set.
- **When:** at a time or after a delay, when the computer has been on for a while, the next time
  the computer is turned on, the next time the program starts, or when a condition becomes true.
  **How often:** once, every N minutes or hours, every day, on chosen days of the week, at every
  start of the program or every time the computer is turned on.
- **Results go to the chat where the task was set.** The message the task writes is marked with
  its due time and how late it ran, and the answer that set a task shows a chip with its name and
  next time.
- **Reminders are cards in the corner** in the program's style: **Done**, **Snooze** (10 minutes,
  1 hour, tomorrow at 9:00) and **Open chat**. A reminder stays until you answer it and comes back
  at the next start if you didn't. Up to three cards are shown at once. When the program is
  locked with a password, the card hides the text.
- **Nothing is lost quietly.** A due time missed while the computer or the program was off runs
  once, marked as late. A task cut short by closing the program asks whether to run it again
  instead of repeating it on its own. A repeating task that fails three times in a row stops and
  says so.
- **The program doesn't need to be open.** While tasks are waiting, Windows Task Scheduler starts
  the program at the due time and when you sign in to Windows, quietly in the tray or minimized.
  The scheduled task is removed when nothing is left to wait for. A profile with a password asks
  for it from a minimized window.
- **Commands are approved when they are set,** in the usual approval window, and *Approve
  everything automatically* or *allow for this chat* never answer for them. A command that was
  changed by hand or came from someone else's archive doesn't run. Read-only mode still applies.
  Conditions may only read. An agent task runs without a plan, with a spending cap of $0.50 per
  run unless the model sets another (up to $5), and stops after two hours.
- **Settings → Automation → Deferred** lists waiting and finished tasks: run now, retry, resume,
  cancel, open the chat.
- **A soft chime** plays for reminders and finished tasks. It is made by the program itself, stays
  silent while Windows is in quiet hours or you present, and can be turned off in **Settings →
  General**, where **Listen** plays it.
- The chat model now knows today's date, so "on Friday" means this Friday.

## Middle-click scrolling

- **Press the mouse wheel** in the conversation, the chat list or Settings: a circle with arrows
  appears where you pressed. Move the mouse away from it and the list scrolls that way, slowly
  near the circle and faster the farther you go. Far enough from the circle, even the longest
  chat goes from the bottom to the top in under a second. Click to stop, or hold the wheel and
  release it.
- Esc stops only the scrolling, not the answer. Any click, the wheel or leaving the window stops
  it too; a right-click stops it without opening a menu.

## Send or move a chat to another profile

- The chat menu has **Send** and **Move** with a list of the other profiles on this computer. The
  chat arrives with its attachments, encrypted if that profile encrypts its chats, at the top of
  its list. Unsent text in the open chat goes along as a draft.
- **Move** removes the chat here only after it is visible in the other profile. A chat that is
  answering right now can't be sent or moved until it finishes. Nothing is written if the other
  profile's chat list can't be read, so its chats are never lost. Success is silent, as when
  sending a key.
